chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: Band style, Louis Jordan's inspiration and early broadcasts
summary: His small entertaining band predates Jordan's; he mentions disc recordings and a number written for Ken Murray.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You were playing basically--were you playing the same style that you had when you started making the records on Decca? Did your style evolve?

I think I was playing the same thing that we made on records, because my idea was to have this small band with arrangements like Trent's, on the idea of entertainment, singing, playing and like Jimmy Lunceford, that's what I wanted.
If you'd a little more luck, you could have gotten what Louis Jordan did.
Let me tell you a funny
about that. I was Louis Jordan's inspiration too. We got down, in the latter part of '37, a club downtown called the Club Afrique, right across from the Harlander (phonetic spelling) Hotel.
Where was that?
43rd and Eighth Avenue. We were downstairs, the guy's name was Posner.
Posner who had the place?
Yeah.
Club Afrique?
Afrique.
I heard of that.

And Louis Jordan was still with Chick Webb, but he came down there and listened. I was entertaining, when a musician comes up I'm going through my motions and then he started that stuff, but he got famous on it. I started the six piece band thing and John

(inaudible) got more credit for it than I did. I played some of my records, in fact, one of the tapes from off of this ABC network, the associated before it got to be ABC, ABS, Associated Broadcasting System, (inaudible).
You got it on a big sixteen inch disc?
I got it on a big disc and I got it on tape too, that I took off the disc.
Give me the disc and I'll take it out to Valburn and get a real good copy from it.
Oh good.
He's the best in the world to do that.
Wonderful.

I got a thing that I wrote about Ken Murray and it comes on the air after I play "Blue Memories" theme song and before you leave, I'd like you to hear it. The Associated Broadcasting System presents (inaudible). He says the first

number is the number that Snub wrote for Ken Murray, especially for Ken Murray who is now listening in in Hollywood, Hopping with Ken Murray, and it was some arrangement. I have a Prelude in C Sharp Minor that has everything on it.
